Bacterial isolate taxonomy from SILVA ACT classification

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source
Author

Shane Hogle

Published

September 27, 2026

Abstract
Parses SILVA ACT classifications of the consensus 16S sequences assembled in 01_sanger_seq/01_trace_qc_assembly.qmd, builds a per-isolate taxonomy table, and summarizes genus/family/phylum composition and phylogeny.

The consensus 16S sequences produced in 01.A Trace QC + assembly were submitted to the SILVA ACT web aligner with LCA classification against SILVA SSU and GTDB enabled. This notebook reads back the two downloaded ACT outputs — the classification result list and the guide tree — and joins them to the per-isolate assembly metadata to build the taxonomy table and summary figures.

1 Setup

1.2 Global variables

Show/hide code

data_processed_sanger <- here::here("data", "processed", "01_sanger_seq")
data_processed <- here::here("data", "processed", "02_bac_taxonomy")

fs::dir_create(data_processed)

2 Read and parse SILVA ACT output

SILVA SSU lineage strings are semicolon-delimited as Domain;<unnamed>;Phylum;Class;Order;Family;Genus, with the second field always empty, and ambiguous LCA nodes suffixed with --other. GTDB lineage strings instead carry g__/s__ prefixed tokens. The two helpers below pull out the ranks we need from each scheme.

Show/hide code 
parse_silva_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  ranks <- c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus")
  rank_idx <- c(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")

  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(
      set_names(as.list(rep(NA_character_, length(ranks))), ranks) |>
        as_tibble()
    )
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]
  parts <- str_remove(parts, "--other")

  vals <- map_chr(
    rank_idx,
    ~ if (length(parts) >= .x) parts[.x] else NA_character_
  )
  set_names(as.list(vals), ranks) |> as_tibble()
}

parse_gtdb_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")
  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(tibble(gtdb_genus = NA_character_, gtdb_species = NA_character_))
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]

  tibble(
    gtdb_genus = parts |>
      str_subset("^g__") |>
      str_remove("^g__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_),
    gtdb_species = parts |>
      str_subset("^s__") |>
      str_remove("^s__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_)
  )
}

Read the result list and apply the parsers row-wise

Show/hide code 
silva_raw <- read_delim(
  silva_resultlist,
  delim = ";",
  quote = '"',
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

silva_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_slv |> map_dfr(parse_silva_taxonomy)
gtdb_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_gtdb |> map_dfr(parse_gtdb_taxonomy)

silva_parsed <- silva_raw |>
  select(
    seq_id = sequence_identifier,
    silva_identity = identity,
    silva_quality = quality,
    silva_score = sequence_score
  ) |>
  bind_cols(silva_tax, gtdb_tax)

3 Build taxonomy table

Join the SILVA classification onto the per-isolate assembly metadata from the trace QC/assembly step

Show/hide code 
assemblies <- read_csv(
  here::here(data_processed_sanger, "assemblies.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

taxonomy_table <- assemblies |>
  select(
    seq_id,
    batch,
    well,
    bacteria_plate_well,
    location,
    google_drive_id,
    assembly_type,
    consensus_length,
    fwd_trimmed_length,
    rev_trimmed_length,
    overlap_length,
    fwd_rev_overlap_identity = overlap_pct_identity
  ) |>
  left_join(silva_parsed, by = "seq_id")

write_csv(
  taxonomy_table,
  here::here(data_processed, "isolate_taxonomy_table.csv")
)
Show/hide code 
n_genus <- sum(!is.na(taxonomy_table$genus))
n_genera <- n_distinct(na.omit(taxonomy_table$genus))
n_unclassified <- sum(is.na(taxonomy_table$domain))
n_gtdb_species <- sum(!is.na(taxonomy_table$gtdb_species))

tibble(
  metric = c(
    "isolates",
    "genus-level calls",
    "distinct genera",
    "unclassified",
    "GTDB species calls"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(taxonomy_table),
    n_genus,
    n_genera,
    n_unclassified,
    n_gtdb_species
  )
)

Below is the compiled taxonomy table: SILVA genotype/quality metrics from the ACT alignment plus domain through genus from the SILVA SSU LCA classification, and gtdb_genus/gtdb_species from the GTDB LCA classification.

Show/hide code 
DT::datatable(
  taxonomy_table,
  class = "cell-border stripe",
  rownames = FALSE,
  extensions = "FixedColumns",
  options = list(
    dom = "ft",
    pageLength = -1,
    scrollX = TRUE,
    fixedColumns = TRUE

)

4 Taxonomy figures

The panels below summarize isolate composition and phylogeny. Each is rendered as its own figure rather than as a combined multi-panel layout; a separate Sanger trace QC figure already lives in the 01.A Trace QC + assembly notebook and isn’t repeated here.

Only isolates with a resolved SILVA SSU classification (domain not missing) are used below

Show/hide code 
classified <- taxonomy_table |> filter(!is.na(domain))

A shared palette for phylum, plus a helper that bins a taxonomic rank into its top categories (grouping everything else as "Other") and computes relative composition per sampling site. Plot styling (theme_project(), capit()) and the make_palette() generator live in R/plotting.R, shared with other notebooks in this project.

Show/hide code 
phylum_colors <- c(
  "Pseudomonadota" = "#1f78b4",
  "Bacteroidota" = "#ff7f00",
  "Bacillota" = "#33a02c",
  "Deinococcota" = "#e31a1c"
)

composition_by_site <- function(
  df,
  rank_col,
  top_n,
  palette,
  other_color = "grey60"
) {
  top_cats <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[rank_col]])) |>
    count(.data[[rank_col]], sort = TRUE) |>
    slice_head(n = top_n) |>
    pull(1)

  plot_df <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(location)) |>
    mutate(
      cat = if_else(.data[[rank_col]] %in% top_cats, .data[[rank_col]], "Other")
    ) |>
    count(location, cat) |>
    group_by(location) |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(cat = factor(cat, levels = c(top_cats, "Other")))

  cat_colors <- c(palette[top_cats], "Other" = other_color)

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = location, y = pct, fill = cat)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cat_colors, name = str_to_title(rank_col)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of isolates") +
    capit() +
    theme_project() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)
    )
}

4.6 Phylogeny

The SILVA ACT guide tree places every isolate among several hundred SILVA reference sequences, which is useful for classification but too dense to read as a figure. For the phylogeny below we root the guide tree on an isolate classified as Lactococcus (the most basal genus recovered, Bacillota) and then prune it down to just our isolates, keeping the topology induced by the full guide tree alignment.

Show/hide code 
tree <- ape::read.tree(silva_tree_file)

outgroup_tip <- classified |>
  filter(genus == outgroup_genus, seq_id %in% tree$tip.label) |>
  pull(seq_id) |>
  pluck(1)

tree_rooted <- ape::root(tree, outgroup = outgroup_tip, resolve.root = TRUE)

isolate_tips <- intersect(tree_rooted$tip.label, classified$seq_id)
tree_pruned <- ape::keep.tip(tree_rooted, isolate_tips)

Every genus recovered among the tree’s isolates gets its own tip color below — nothing is pooled into an “Other” category. Class-level groups are additionally marked with a ggtree::geom_cladelab() bracket. geom_cladelab() needs a single tree node spanning exactly the tips being labeled, but because this is a guide tree built for alignment across hundreds of SILVA references rather than a phylogeny inferred from just our isolates, a class doesn’t always come out as a clean monophyletic clade after pruning. The helper below finds, for a given set of tips, the largest node whose full descendant set is “pure” (i.e. contains only members of that class and nothing else) — the clade that gets labeled — and reports how many of the class’s tips that clade actually covers.

Show/hide code 
node_tip_set <- function(tree, node) {
  ntip <- length(tree$tip.label)
  if (node <= ntip) {
    return(tree$tip.label[node])
  }
  ape::extract.clade(tree, node)$tip.label
}

largest_pure_clade <- function(tree, target_tips) {
  n_total <- length(target_tips)

  if (n_total == 1) {
    return(tibble(
      node = which(tree$tip.label == target_tips),
      n_covered = 1L,
      n_total = 1L
    ))
  }

  ntip <- length(tree$tip.label)
  internal_nodes <- seq(ntip + 1, ntip + tree$Nnode)
  sizes <- map_int(internal_nodes, function(nd) {
    desc <- node_tip_set(tree, nd)
    if (all(desc %in% target_tips)) length(desc) else NA_integer_
  })

  if (all(is.na(sizes))) {
    return(tibble(node = NA_integer_, n_covered = 0L, n_total = n_total))
  }

  best_idx <- which.max(sizes)
  tibble(
    node = internal_nodes[best_idx],
    n_covered = sizes[best_idx],
    n_total = n_total
  )
}

class_groups <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips, !is.na(class)) |>
  summarise(members = list(seq_id), .by = class) |>
  mutate(clade = map(members, ~ largest_pure_clade(tree_pruned, .x))) |>
  unnest(clade) |>
  select(-members) |>
  filter(!is.na(node))
Show/hide code 
n_class_partial <- sum(class_groups$n_covered != class_groups$n_total)

All 5 classes recovered are labeled; 1 of them (Bacilli, whose Lactococcus and Exiguobacterium members don’t share a single common ancestor exclusive of other classes here) is only partially monophyletic, so its bracket covers just the largest pure block.

Show/hide code 
all_genus_tree <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips, !is.na(genus)) |>
  distinct(genus) |>
  arrange(genus) |>
  pull(genus)

genus_tree_pal <- make_palette(all_genus_tree)

tip_data <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips) |>
  transmute(label = seq_id, genus_grp = coalesce(genus, "Unclassified"))
Show/hide code 
ggtree(tree_pruned, layout = "rectangular") %<+%
  tip_data +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = genus_grp), size = 1.5) +
  geom_tiplab(size = 2, hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(genus_tree_pal, "Unclassified" = "grey50"),
    name = "Genus"
  ) +
  geom_cladelab(
    node = class_groups$node,
    label = class_groups$class,
    align = TRUE,
    geom = "text",
    offset = 0.9,
    offset.text = 0.05,
    fontsize = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    barsize = 0.6
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  ggplot2::xlim(NA, 4) +
  geom_treescale(offset = 1)

The consensus 16S sequences produced in [01.A Trace QC + assembly](../01_sanger_seq/01_trace_qc_assembly.qmd) were submitted to the [SILVA ACT web aligner](https://www.arb-silva.de/aligner) with LCA classification against SILVA SSU and GTDB enabled. This notebook reads back the two downloaded ACT outputs — the classification result list and the guide tree — and joins them to the per-isolate assembly metadata to build the taxonomy table and summary figures.

# Setup

## Libraries

Loads required libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

library(ape)
library(treeio)
library(ggtree)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(Polychrome)
library(DT)

source(here::here("R", "plotting.R"))
```

## Global variables

```{r}
data_raw <- here::here("data", "raw", "20260908_silva_act")
data_processed_sanger <- here::here("data", "processed", "01_sanger_seq")
data_processed <- here::here("data", "processed", "02_bac_taxonomy")

fs::dir_create(data_processed)

silva_resultlist <- here::here(
  data_raw,
  "arb-silva.de_align_resultlist_1508237.csv"
)
silva_tree_file <- here::here(
  data_raw,
  "arb-silva.de_2026-09-08_id1508237.tree"
)

outgroup_genus <- "Lactococcus"
```

# Read and parse SILVA ACT output

SILVA SSU lineage strings are semicolon-delimited as `Domain;<unnamed>;Phylum;Class;Order;Family;Genus`, with the second field always empty, and ambiguous LCA nodes suffixed with `--other`. GTDB lineage strings instead carry `g__`/`s__` prefixed tokens. The two helpers below pull out the ranks we need from each scheme.

```{r}
parse_silva_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  ranks <- c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus")
  rank_idx <- c(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")

  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(
      set_names(as.list(rep(NA_character_, length(ranks))), ranks) |>
        as_tibble()
    )
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]
  parts <- str_remove(parts, "--other")

  vals <- map_chr(
    rank_idx,
    ~ if (length(parts) >= .x) parts[.x] else NA_character_
  )
  set_names(as.list(vals), ranks) |> as_tibble()
}

parse_gtdb_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")
  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(tibble(gtdb_genus = NA_character_, gtdb_species = NA_character_))
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]

  tibble(
    gtdb_genus = parts |>
      str_subset("^g__") |>
      str_remove("^g__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_),
    gtdb_species = parts |>
      str_subset("^s__") |>
      str_remove("^s__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_)
  )
}
```

Read the result list and apply the parsers row-wise

```{r}
silva_raw <- read_delim(
  silva_resultlist,
  delim = ";",
  quote = '"',
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

silva_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_slv |> map_dfr(parse_silva_taxonomy)
gtdb_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_gtdb |> map_dfr(parse_gtdb_taxonomy)

silva_parsed <- silva_raw |>
  select(
    seq_id = sequence_identifier,
    silva_identity = identity,
    silva_quality = quality,
    silva_score = sequence_score
  ) |>
  bind_cols(silva_tax, gtdb_tax)
```

# Build taxonomy table

Join the SILVA classification onto the per-isolate assembly metadata from the trace QC/assembly step

```{r}
assemblies <- read_csv(
  here::here(data_processed_sanger, "assemblies.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

taxonomy_table <- assemblies |>
  select(
    seq_id,
    batch,
    well,
    bacteria_plate_well,
    location,
    google_drive_id,
    assembly_type,
    consensus_length,
    fwd_trimmed_length,
    rev_trimmed_length,
    overlap_length,
    fwd_rev_overlap_identity = overlap_pct_identity
  ) |>
  left_join(silva_parsed, by = "seq_id")

write_csv(
  taxonomy_table,
  here::here(data_processed, "isolate_taxonomy_table.csv")
)
```

```{r}
#| output: true
n_genus <- sum(!is.na(taxonomy_table$genus))
n_genera <- n_distinct(na.omit(taxonomy_table$genus))
n_unclassified <- sum(is.na(taxonomy_table$domain))
n_gtdb_species <- sum(!is.na(taxonomy_table$gtdb_species))

tibble(
  metric = c(
    "isolates",
    "genus-level calls",
    "distinct genera",
    "unclassified",
    "GTDB species calls"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(taxonomy_table),
    n_genus,
    n_genera,
    n_unclassified,
    n_gtdb_species
```

```{r}
)
```

# Taxonomy figures

The panels below summarize isolate composition and phylogeny. Each is rendered as its own figure rather than as a combined multi-panel layout; a separate Sanger trace QC figure already lives in the [01.A Trace QC + assembly](../01_sanger_seq/01_trace_qc_assembly.qmd) notebook and isn't repeated here.

Only isolates with a resolved SILVA SSU classification (`domain` not missing) are used below

```{r}
classified <- taxonomy_table |> filter(!is.na(domain))
```

A shared palette for phylum, plus a helper that bins a taxonomic rank into its top categories (grouping everything else as `"Other"`) and computes relative composition per sampling site. Plot styling (`theme_project()`, `capit()`) and the `make_palette()` generator live in [`R/plotting.R`](../../R/plotting.R), shared with other notebooks in this project.

```{r}
phylum_colors <- c(
  "Pseudomonadota" = "#1f78b4",
  "Bacteroidota" = "#ff7f00",
  "Bacillota" = "#33a02c",
  "Deinococcota" = "#e31a1c"
)

composition_by_site <- function(
  df,
  rank_col,
  top_n,
  palette,
  other_color = "grey60"
) {
  top_cats <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[rank_col]])) |>
    count(.data[[rank_col]], sort = TRUE) |>
    slice_head(n = top_n) |>
    pull(1)

  plot_df <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(location)) |>
    mutate(
      cat = if_else(.data[[rank_col]] %in% top_cats, .data[[rank_col]], "Other")
    ) |>
    count(location, cat) |>
    group_by(location) |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(cat = factor(cat, levels = c(top_cats, "Other")))

  cat_colors <- c(palette[top_cats], "Other" = other_color)

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = location, y = pct, fill = cat)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cat_colors, name = str_to_title(rank_col)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of isolates") +
    capit() +
    theme_project() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)
    )
}
```

## Genus composition across all isolates

```{r}
genus_counts <- classified |> count(genus, sort = TRUE)

top_genus <- genus_counts |> filter(!is.na(genus)) |> slice_head(n = 12)
other_n <- genus_counts |>
  filter(!genus %in% top_genus$genus | is.na(genus)) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n)) |>
  pull(n)

genus_plot_df <- bind_rows(top_genus, tibble(genus = "Other", n = other_n)) |>
  mutate(genus = fct_reorder(genus, n))
```

```{r}

  geom_col(fill = "#1f78b4") +
```

## Phylogeny

The SILVA ACT guide tree places every isolate among several hundred SILVA reference sequences, which is useful for classification but too dense to read as a figure. For the phylogeny below we root the guide tree on an isolate classified as *Lactococcus* (the most basal genus recovered, Bacillota) and then prune it down to just our isolates, keeping the topology induced by the full guide tree alignment.

```{r}
tree <- ape::read.tree(silva_tree_file)

outgroup_tip <- classified |>
  filter(genus == outgroup_genus, seq_id %in% tree$tip.label) |>
  pull(seq_id) |>
  pluck(1)

tree_rooted <- ape::root(tree, outgroup = outgroup_tip, resolve.root = TRUE)

isolate_tips <- intersect(tree_rooted$tip.label, classified$seq_id)
tree_pruned <- ape::keep.tip(tree_rooted, isolate_tips)
```

Every genus recovered among the tree's isolates gets its own tip color below — nothing is pooled into an "Other" category. Class-level groups are additionally marked with a `ggtree::geom_cladelab()` bracket. `geom_cladelab()` needs a single tree node spanning exactly the tips being labeled, but because this is a guide tree built for alignment across hundreds of SILVA references rather than a phylogeny inferred from just our isolates, a class doesn't always come out as a clean monophyletic clade after pruning. The helper below finds, for a given set of tips, the largest node whose full descendant set is "pure" (i.e. contains only members of that class and nothing else) — the clade that gets labeled — and reports how many of the class's tips that clade actually covers.

```{r}
node_tip_set <- function(tree, node) {
  ntip <- length(tree$tip.label)
  if (node <= ntip) {
    return(tree$tip.label[node])
  }
  ape::extract.clade(tree, node)$tip.label
}

largest_pure_clade <- function(tree, target_tips) {
  n_total <- length(target_tips)

  if (n_total == 1) {
    return(tibble(
      node = which(tree$tip.label == target_tips),
      n_covered = 1L,
      n_total = 1L
    ))
  }

  ntip <- length(tree$tip.label)
  internal_nodes <- seq(ntip + 1, ntip + tree$Nnode)
  sizes <- map_int(internal_nodes, function(nd) {
    desc <- node_tip_set(tree, nd)
    if (all(desc %in% target_tips)) length(desc) else NA_integer_
  })

  if (all(is.na(sizes))) {
    return(tibble(node = NA_integer_, n_covered = 0L, n_total = n_total))
  }

  best_idx <- which.max(sizes)
  tibble(
    node = internal_nodes[best_idx],
    n_covered = sizes[best_idx],
    n_total = n_total
  )
}

class_groups <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips, !is.na(class)) |>
  summarise(members = list(seq_id), .by = class) |>
  mutate(clade = map(members, ~ largest_pure_clade(tree_pruned, .x))) |>
  unnest(clade) |>
  select(-members) |>
  filter(!is.na(node))
```

```{r}
n_class_partial <- sum(class_groups$n_covered != class_groups$n_total)
```

All `r nrow(class_groups)` classes recovered are labeled; `r n_class_partial` of them (*Bacilli*, whose *Lactococcus* and *Exiguobacterium* members don't share a single common ancestor exclusive of other classes here) is only partially monophyletic, so its bracket covers just the largest pure block.

```{r}
all_genus_tree <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips, !is.na(genus)) |>
  distinct(genus) |>
  arrange(genus) |>
  pull(genus)

genus_tree_pal <- make_palette(all_genus_tree)

tip_data <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips) |>
  transmute(label = seq_id, genus_grp = coalesce(genus, "Unclassified"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tree
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 22
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Phylogeny of the ", length(isolate_tips), " classified isolates, pruned from the SILVA ACT guide tree and rooted on an isolate classified as *Lactococcus*. Tip points are colored by genus, with every genus recovered (", length(all_genus_tree), ') shown individually; isolates with a domain-level SILVA classification but no resolved genus are labeled "Unclassified". Bracketed labels on the right mark class-level membership (`ggtree::geom_cladelab()`). Scale bar represents substitutions per site.')
ggtree(tree_pruned, layout = "rectangular") %<+%
  tip_data +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = genus_grp), size = 1.5) +
  geom_tiplab(size = 2, hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(genus_tree_pal, "Unclassified" = "grey50"),
    name = "Genus"
  ) +
  geom_cladelab(
    node = class_groups$node,
    label = class_groups$class,
    align = TRUE,
    geom = "text",
    offset = 0.9,
    offset.text = 0.05,
    fontsize = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    barsize = 0.6
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  ggplot2::xlim(NA, 4) +
  geom_treescale(offset = 1)
```
